messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] Dedicated pool 'peregrine-prod-1' high GPU saturation. Tenant="Peregrine Health". GPU queueing 420 requests, avg GPU util 97%. Paging on-call SRE. https://redwood/status/5167890123

sre_zoe: oncall here, looking into it. reassigning to oncall_aaron for mitigation.

oncall_aaron: I'm up. admit I'm seeing heavy queueing and rising latencies. Any customer reports?

eng_runtime_sam: I have a read on metrics — pool peregrine-prod-1 (8xA100) is saturated. Peregrine tenant showing ~75% of tokens served, lots of long-running chat sessions keeping KV cache hot. Autoscaler didn't add GPUs because burst limit for this tenant = 0 (billing guardrail).

support_julia: Peregrine Health reports many 504s and timeouts, their web UI is timing out on generation step. They're on a live demo at 11:00 PDT and are escalating. I've put them on a high-touch bridge.

am_lee: customer confirmed demo in ~35m. Need fast mitigation, please advise next steps and risks.

eng_runtime_sam: Options (fast --> slower):
1) temporary manual burst override: +3 GPUs to pool. Quick but requires platform approval (billing/ops).
2) enable tenant-level concurrency throttle (eg limit active streams to 2) — near-zero infra risk, immediate.
3) enable QoS eviction for non-marked jobs (evict low-priority jobs from Peregrine). Could drop some background evals.
4) fallback routing: shift a fraction of requests to hosted variant (smaller model) — requires config change and customer consent for quality drop.

sre_zoe: I'll implement option 2 now (concurrency throttle) and option 3 as backup. Aaron can you validate traffic shaping?

oncall_aaron: running throttle script now. Command: ```./infra-tools throttle-tenant --tenant peregrine-health --concurrency 2 --reason "incident 5167890123"```

incident-bot: Action recorded: throttle applied by oncall_aaron at 5167890450. New active streams for tenant capped at 2.

eng_runtime_sam: Seeing queue depth drop from 420 -> 120 within 90s. GPU util down to 82%. Latency p50 improving.

support_julia: Customer reports partial improvement, some long-generation jobs still failing but overall throughput is better. They appreciate the quick fix.

am_lee: Good. Can we still add burst GPUs? They want demo unaffected.

eng_platform_maya: I can approve a one-time burst of up to +4 GPUs for this pool, but need AM confirmation to proceed with billing override. Cost center?

am_lee: Approving on behalf of the account. AM confirms they accept temporary cost for demo. Please proceed.

eng_platform_maya: Manual burst initiated at 5167891200: +3 GPUs added to peregrine-prod-1. Monitoring now.

incident-bot: Action recorded: manual-burst +3 by eng_platform_maya at 5167891200.

eng_runtime_sam: After burst, queue depth down to 18, GPU util 45%, p95 latency back to baseline for most requests. A handful of long KV-cache-heavy sessions still show higher latency — throttled those sessions manually.

support_julia: Customer confirms demo resumed, latency improved. They asked whether this could recur.

oncall_aaron: Short-term mitigations applied: throttle + manual burst + evictions for non-critical jobs.

eng_runtime_sam: Action items:
- Short: keep burst for 2 hours, monitor (sam).
- Medium: adjust tenant burst quota and add dynamic QoS to avoid single-tenant takeover (platform/maya).
- Long: postmortem + perf playbook for enterprise demos (owner: sam).

incident-bot: Incident severity set to P1-customer-impact. Postmortem owner assigned: eng_runtime_sam.

customer_ops_tom: I'll send a recap to Peregrine Health and offer a mitigation plan.

sre_zoe: handing off to daytime oncall. If anything regresses tag #peregrine-incident.

am_lee: Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

eng_runtime_sam: Logging follow-ups in Jira: RDW-1429 (tenant burst quotas), RDW-1430 (QoS eviction config), RDW-1431 (demo runbook).
